extracted.intended_audience: healthcare providers and suppliers (including Medicare Part B providers), CMS-regulated entities, state Medicaid agencies, managed care plans, PACE organizations, health insurers/QHP issuers, Exchange administrators, and compliance/legal officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and interpretive guidance implementing section 1557 and related HHS/CMS nondiscrimination rules for health programs and activities, including the treatment of Medicare Part B as Federal financial assistance and amendments to Medicaid/CHIP, PACE, and Exchange-related regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform nondiscrimination phrasing across regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Revising §92.304(a) and (b) to read '... discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any combination thereof ...' and replacing cross-referenced uses of the term 'handicap' with the phrase 'race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aligns wording with edits made at §§92.101(a)(1), 92.207(a) and (b)(1) and (2), and 92.303(a) to ensure consistent terminology across the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of section 504 procedural provisions to administrative enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide that the procedural provisions applicable to section 504 at 45 CFR 85.61 and 85.62 shall apply with respect to administrative enforcement actions against the Department, including Federally-facilitated Exchanges, concerning discrimination under section 1557 or the part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clarity and consistency, administrative enforcement against the Department and Exchanges will follow these established procedural provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Part B qualifies as Federal financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is finalizing its interpretation that Medicare Part B ('Part B') funding meets the definition of 'Federal financial assistance' for purposes of title VI, title IX, section 504, the Age Act, and section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B funds are considered Federal financial assistance when received by providers and suppliers because Part B confers a benefit or subsidy on the recipient (financial assistance to the provider in exchange for providing services), and many providers are paid directly by the Medicare program. This interprets 'Federal financial assistance' consistently with prior treatment of Medicare Part A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and delayed applicability for newly covered Part B-only recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: The interpretation that Part B constitutes Federal financial assistance is effective upon Federal Register publication, but has a one-year delayed applicability date for entities whose Federal program participation has been limited to Part B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities newly required to comply must be in compliance no later than May 6, 2025. An Assurance of Compliance (45 CFR 92.5) must be filed with the Department by those entities no later than that date via OCR's Assurance of Compliance portal (https://ocrportal.hhs.gov/ocr/aoc/instruction.jsf). If a recipient accepts other Federal financial assistance prior to May 6, 2025, it must complete an Assurance of Compliance at that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of technical assistance to newly covered entities
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR will provide adequate support and technical assistance to entities newly covered by section 1557 due to the Part B designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department amended the applicability date to give such recipients sufficient time to come into compliance and will provide resources to assist newly covered entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'sex' in CMS regulations includes specific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS regulations are revised so that discrimination based on 'sex' includes discrimination based on sex characteristics, including intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity, including transgender status; and sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is not exhaustive but provides explicit examples to avoid confusion and ensure consistency with 45 CFR 92.101(a)(2). Adopting identical language across CMS and section 1557 helps regulated entities comply and promotes consistent enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text as examples, not exhaustive limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The examples listed in the regulation text (sex characteristics, intersex traits, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, sex stereotypes) are illustrative and not the only ways that discrimination can be based on sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities should interpret the regulation broadly — the regulation identifies examples; enforcement or compliance is not limited to those examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to provide specific services or treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule does not (and cannot) require a specific standard of care or course of treatment for any individual, minor or adult, and does not require entities to cover any particular procedure or treatment (including gender-affirming care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These nondiscrimination provisions are neutral and generally applicable; they prohibit discriminatory conduct but do not mandate coverage of particular items/services. Conduct is not a violation if there is a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for the action and decisions may be individualized based on current medical standards and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for religious freedom and conscience protections in enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: When enforcing nondiscrimination regulations, HHS will comply with laws protecting the exercise of conscience and religion, including the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA) and all other applicable legal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The nondiscrimination provisions do not displace protections for religious freedom and conscience; enforcement actions will account for these statutory protections. Physician licensing and discipline remain outside the scope of this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of Medicaid/CHIP managed care and fee-for-service language
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments restore and align regulatory text in 42 CFR 438.3(d)(4), 438.206(c)(2), and 440.262 (and corresponding CHIP cross-references) to prohibit discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity and to require promotion of access and delivery of services in a culturally competent manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency between managed care and fee-for-service programs (and with section 1557) facilitates simplicity of administration and protects beneficiaries across Medicaid delivery systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: States' prospective and retrospective monitoring responsibilities (42 CFR 438.66)
rubrics_metrics.description: States must have a monitoring system for all Medicaid managed care programs that addresses all aspects of the program including the performance of each managed care plan, and must use data collected from monitoring activities to improve program performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This state monitoring requirement demonstrates how Medicaid managed care regulations provide prospective and retrospective compliance mechanisms to complement OCR's enforcement of nondiscrimination prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change 'unique' to 'individualized' to reflect person-centered care
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision of 42 CFR 440.262 replaces the word 'unique' with 'individualized' to more accurately reflect Medicaid's goal of providing person-centered care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording better captures the expectation that services and access should be tailored to individuals rather than labeled merely 'unique.'

rubrics_metrics.name: PACE nondiscrimination protections expanded
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 42 CFR 460.98(b)(3) and 42 CFR 460.112 to add sexual orientation and gender identity to the list of characteristics that may not serve as a basis for discrimination against a PACE participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These PACE provisions become applicable one year after the effective date of the final rule. The rule clarifies it does not require PACE organizations to include coverage for any particular item or service not already covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination in Exchanges, QHPs, and issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed and finalized amendments to Exchange- and issuer-related rules prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity for Exchanges, QHPs, and certain issuers and their officials, employees, agents, and representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amendments are intended to align Exchange and issuer obligations with section 1557 nondiscrimination protections and to improve clarity and enforcement across settings where program-specific rules may be more visible to regulated entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If any provision of this final rule is held invalid or unenforceable by its terms, or as applied to any person or circumstance, or stayed pending further action, it shall be severable from this final rule and not affect the remainder thereof or other persons/circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions are intended to operate independently; where a provision depends on another, the context generally makes that clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct does not constitute a violation of the prohibition on sex discrimination if there is a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities may take nondiscriminatory actions based on current medical standards and evidence (e.g., individualized determinations about timing or type of protocols appropriate for care) without those actions being deemed unlawful discrimination under these rules.
